findings.severity: blocks a designed state from reaching the client
findings.statement: DigitalOcean App Platform's Cloudflare-backed ingress replaces ANY 5xx response from the app with its own 1263-byte text/html page and a 504 status, dropping the body; the origin status survives only in the X-Do-Orig-Status header. DigitalOcean support has confirmed this is enforced by the Cloudflare integration and cannot be changed per app.

evidenceFor.appThatAnswered: walrus-app's own RUN log shows the app answering 'GET /api/platform/firstdue/apparatus 503 in 197ms :: {"error":"permission_required"...}' and 'GET /api/platform/goto/call-summary 503 in 2ms :: {"error":"goto_not_authorized"...}' at the timestamps of these very probes
evidenceFor.clientSaw: 504, content-type text/html, 1263 bytes, server: cloudflare, answered in 125-487ms (an edge refusal, not an origin timeout)
evidenceFor.reproducedOn: two independent apps running the same commit (walrus-app and d14-main-proof), and on both public hostnames
evidenceFor.controlThatSeparatesIt: an UNAUTHENTICATED request to the same two paths returns the app's own 401 JSON unchanged through the same edge, and the healthy samsara feed returns 200 through the same edge — so 2xx and 4xx pass and only 5xx is replaced
evidenceFor.notTheApp: the GCP v1 copy, which is not behind this ingress, returns the same two 503 JSON refusals normally

unauth4xxControlCells.vantage: assembled on the lane host, no credential sent
unauth4xxControlCells.whatItShows: an unauthenticated request to the very same two paths returns the app's own 401 JSON with x-do-orig-status=401 through the same Cloudflare edge. 2xx and 4xx pass through; only 5xx is replaced.
unauth4xxControlCells.walrusRowAbsentBecause: every fetch to walrus-app from THIS host failed at the transport ('TypeError: fetch failed') while d14-main-proof, d12-main-uat and the GCP host all answered from the same process, so the row is omitted rather than shown as a failure of the app. It is not needed: walrus-app's half of the same control is measured in authenticated5xxCells below from the Cloud Build vantage, where its healthy samsara control returns 200.

authenticated5xxCells.vantage: GCP Cloud Build, PLATFORM_INTERNAL_API_KEY injected from Secret Manager (OPS-25 rule 10)
authenticated5xxCells.theDecisiveField: x-do-orig-status carries the status the APPLICATION sent. Every 504/text-html cell below reads x-do-orig-status=503: the app answered 503 and the ingress delivered 504 with the body dropped.

applicationSideOfTheSameRequests.vantage: walrus-app's own DigitalOcean RUN log, read through the DigitalOcean API
applicationSideOfTheSameRequests.whyThisMatters: the timestamps are the probe's own requests, so the same request is recorded twice: the app logging a named 503, and the client receiving a nameless 504.

findings.consequence: the two feeds whose honest state is a NAMED vendor refusal (FirstDue 503 permission_required, GoTo 503 goto_not_authorized) cannot deliver that name to a client on DigitalOcean. The vendor-blocked boards the G-152 designs draw — which say a vendor entitlement, not a bug, is the obstacle — receive unparseable HTML instead of the reason. This is a pre-existing platform behaviour, not something the repoint introduced, but the repoint is what moves the dashboards onto the platform that has it.
findings.remedyDirection: do not carry a DECLARED terminal refusal on a 5xx status; the named refusal must ride a status the ingress passes (a 4xx, as G-161's city_key_required already does) or a header. This is a dashboards design/instrument decision, not a smartcity-os one, and it is carded rather than fixed here.

findings.statement: once D-13.1 is on main, any dolphin-app deploy that does not also carry SMARTCITY_V1_PLATFORM_BASE fails closed on every feed: platformRoute returns null and each feed refuses with its basis stated rather than falling back to the retired GCP host. That is deliberate.
